There are multiple ways to motivate this problem: (1) in many settings the contamination happens before some noise is added to the data, e.g., the max-affine regression problem as it is described in [ li2023thesis ] , and (2) in large-scale multiple testing most samples follow a null distribution centered at an unknown mean, and a minority arise from shifted alternatives. This setting, studied in [ carpentier2021estimating , kotekal2025optimal , diakonikolas2025efficient ] and it is related to empirical Bayes’ models of [ efron2004large ] . Finally, the noise-oblivious contamination model is a classical instance of learning from heterogeneous data [ compton2024near ] , where samples are drawn independently, but from non-identical distributions. We refer to Section 1.5 for a more detailed comparison with previous work. Our results. Our final result is to show that, under the Slow Fourier Decay condition, our Fourier-based technique implies an efficient algorithm with polynomial sample complexity to solve the mean estimation problem with noise-oblivious contamination.
